pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = }} '''''Athlitiki Enosi Larissa Football Club''''' ({{langx|el|ΠΑΕ ΑΕΛ – Αθλητικής Ένωσης Λάρισας|Athlitiki Enosi Larissa|translation=Athletic Union of Larissa}}), often known as '''AEL''' or '''Larissa''', and '''''AEL Novibet''''' for sponsorship reasons,{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/16472159|title=Chris Coleman leaves troubled Greece club Larissa|date=9 January 2012|access-date=21 May 2018|work=BBC Sport}} is a Greek professional [[Association football|football]] club based in the city of [[Larissa]], capital of Greece's [[Thessaly]] region.{{Cite journal |last=Enosi |first=Buluma |date=2021-06-17 |title=network topology |url=https://doi.org/10.20935/al1194 |journal=Academia Letters |doi=10.20935/al1194 |issn=2771-9359|url-access=subscription }} Founded in 1964, when 4 of the most prominent local football clubs decided to unite, it is directly associated with the city of [[Larissa]] and its representation. The club's emblem, is a rising [[horse]] and its colors are [[crimson]] and [[white]]. It is the only team based outside of the major Greek cities ([[Athens]] and [[Thessaloniki]]) to have won the Greek [[Championship]], which happened in the 1987–88 season. AEL has also won the [[Greek Cup]] twice (1984–85 and 2006–07) and came runners-up in the Cup finals of 1982 and 1984.Is the second biggest club outside Athens and Thessaloniki.OFI Crete is the biggest one.The team is followed by a loud and loyal fanbase, and has a strong rivalry with other big teams in Greece, such as [[PAOK FC|PAOK]] and [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]].{{Cite web |last=Li |first=Fei-Ju |last2=Starrs |first2=Lora |last3=Mathur |first3=Anukriti |last4=Enosi Tuipulotu |first4=Daniel |last5=Man |first5=Si Ming |last6=Burgio |first6=Gaetan |date=2022-10-25 |title=GBP1 promotes killing of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii and promotes host protection via interferon signalling and inflammasome activation |url=https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.10.24.513490 |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=doi.org}} AEL had also participated in European competitions, reaching the league phase of [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] in 2007-2008. Most notably, it has reached the quarter finals of the [[UEFA Cup Winner's Cup]] during the 1984–85 season. AEL play their home games at [[AEL FC Arena]], a pure football ground with a capacity of 17,118 seats which can expand to 33,000 making it the third largest [[Stadium]] in Greece."}}
